english.title: Fail to retain documentation relating to the supply / receipt of a class POM-V / POM-VPS vet medicinal product
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person who was permitted under the Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2013 to supply a veterinary medicinal product classified as POM-V or POM-VPS and who received or supplied such a product, failed to keep all documents relating to the transaction for five years and in accordance with regulation 23 of the said regulations in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 23, 43(o) and 44(1) of the Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2013.

english.notes: From the 17th May 2024, this offence no longer applies due to changes made by the Veterinary Medicines (Amendment etc.) Regulations 2024. For the offence applying from this date, see H101682.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
